assumptions.name: beta
assumptions.justification: Regressed against S&P 500 on monthly total returns to 2026-09-17, over 72 paired observations. The proxy and the window are both judgements and both change the answer, which is why this is a proposal rather than an input.

assumptions.name: capex_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of capital expenditure over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. The individual observations were 0.0292, 0.0246, 0.0297, 0.0356, 0.0478.

assumptions.name: depreciation_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of depreciation and amortisation over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. The individual observations were 0.1745, 0.1236, 0.1017, 0.0873, 0.0866.

assumptions.name: ebit_margin
assumptions.justification: The mean of operating income over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. The individual observations were 0.0282, 0.0847, 0.1788, 0.1850, 0.2340.

assumptions.name: exit_multiple
assumptions.justification: Grounded in the derived intensities: mean EBIT margin 14.2% plus D&A intensity 11.5% implies an EBITDA margin near 26%, of which capex (3.3%) and cash tax absorb a modest share, so a mature diversified pharma converting most EBITDA to cash supports a low-double-digit multiple. 12x is broadly consistent with 2.5% perpetual growth at a 8-8.5% discount rate. It is partly a sector convention and I flag that. Of the two, I regard the perpetual-growth figure as the better terminal-value estimate here, because AZN's amortisation intensity (11.5% of revenue) is largely acquired-intangible cost that EV/EBITDA ignores, flattering the multiple. A clearer post-2030 patent-cliff picture would move this either way.

assumptions.name: revenue_growth
assumptions.justification: The compound annual growth rate of revenue from 2021-12-31 to 2025-12-31, over 4 year(s): revenue moved from 37,417,000,000 to 58,739,000,000. Held flat across the forecast, because a trailing rate is one number and projecting a fade is a judgement this derivation does not make.

assumptions.name: risk_free_rate
assumptions.justification: The US 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield was 5% on 2026-09-15, as published by 2026-09-17 (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15), series DGS10). Taken as the USD risk-free rate for this run's as-of date and converted to the fraction 0.05.

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.justification: Taken as below a cost of capital of at least 7.5-8% (5.0% derived risk-free plus any ordinary equity premium for a large-cap pharma), so it holds below any plausible discount rate for this run. 2.5% reflects nominal global healthcare spend rather than AZN's trailing 11.9% revenue CAGR, which is launch-driven and cannot persist: the filings show newer patent-protected brands (Enhertu, Tagrisso, Imfinzi) alongside off-patent Nexium/Crestor/Pulmicort, i.e. perpetual reinvestment merely to replace eroding revenue. The SERENA-4 primary-endpoint miss is a reminder that pipeline replacement is uncertain. Evidence of durable pricing power or a structurally broader label set would support a higher figure; sustained US/EU reimbursement pressure a lower one.

assumptions.name: working_capital_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of net working capital — current assets less current liabilities — over revenue, across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. A negative figure is normal for a business paid before it pays, and is proposed as it stands rather than floored at zero.
